description:
The project-lead skill's prompts and reference templates name the canonical artifact directory instead of a flat short-id-prefixed path, and each packaged profile twin carries the identical content.

## Background

This skill already composes its roots from configuration rather than hard-coding them, so what remains is the artifact-name shape: progress files, charters, and the standards-sweep report are still spelled out as a root joined with a short-id-prefixed filename. Two of its references already name hard-coded roots as a mistake, so this generalizes a rule the prompts already state.

The affected files are declared assets of a packaged profile and are asserted byte-identical to their packaged copies, so each edit travels with its twin or the suite fails.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: No prompt or reference in this skill instructs a reader to compose an issue artifact path from a flat area-plus-short-id-prefix pattern.
- [hard] REQ-02: An instruction that names an artifact filename uses an unprefixed filename inside the resolved directory.
- [hard] REQ-03: No instruction derives an artifact directory or filename from an issue title.
- [hard] REQ-04: Each edited file that is a declared profile asset is byte-identical to its packaged twin, including file mode.
- [hard] REQ-05: Evaluation fixtures, transcripts, and worktree directory patterns in this skill are unchanged.
title: Convert the project-lead skill to the artifact directory convention
